# Clanker operator setup

For agent-guided setup, paste the [setup prompt](SETUP_PROMPT.md) into your coding
agent with this repository open. This guide describes the current local POC.
Complete browser activation on a clean machine still needs verification.

## Runtime and model

Install the pinned environment using the [installation guide](INSTALL.md). The launcher creates
`.local/hermes-lab/home/config.yaml` from the initial baseline only if it does not
already exist. It also creates a mode-600 `.env`. Configure inference interactively
with `scripts/hermes-lab model`, preserving `auth.adopt_external_logins: false`.

Current development uses `gpt-6.1-sol` through `openai-codex`. A new operator must
authorize their own eligible account or choose another Hermes-supported provider.
Do not copy development authentication into a submission or another installation.

## Slack app and membership

Create the app from the [manifest](../config/slack-app-manifest.json),
enable Socket Mode, create an app-level token with `connections:write`, and
install the bot in the intended workspace. Record the workspace ID and operator
member ID from Slack. Put the real tokens only in the local `.env`:

```dotenv
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=REPLACE_LOCALLY_WITH_BOT_TOKEN
SLACK_APP_TOKEN=REPLACE_LOCALLY_WITH_SOCKET_MODE_TOKEN
```

Merge this configuration into `.local/hermes-lab/home/config.yaml`, replacing
both ID placeholders. Preserve the model and baseline security/display settings:

```yaml
gateway:
  multiplex_profiles: true
  platforms:
    slack:
      skip_context_files: true

slack:
  require_mention: true
  unauthorized_dm_behavior: ignore

platforms:
  slack:
    enabled: true
    gateway_restart_notification: false
    typing_indicator: true
    extra:
      allow_admin_from:
        - OPERATOR_MEMBER_ID
      group_allow_admin_from:
        - OPERATOR_MEMBER_ID
      user_allowed_commands:
        - status
        - stop
      group_user_allowed_commands:
        - status
        - stop
      reactions: true
      acknowledgement_reactions: true
      workspace_membership:
        enabled: true
        workspace_id: WORKSPACE_TEAM_ID

platform_toolsets:
  cli: []
  slack: []
```

Starting with empty toolsets keeps chat available while execution is being
prepared. The verified execution plugin supplies `clanker_browser` only after
activation; adding that name by itself does not install or verify a browser.

For a fresh installation, the controller provisions eligible current workspace
members into new profiles. Existing installations may use an explicit
`workspace_membership.existing_profiles` mapping, but must verify those profiles'
ownership before reusing them. The configured workspace and current channel/bot
membership govern admission; an old owner-only `SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS` or channel
allowlist can prevent the intended member experience. Review existing restrictions
deliberately rather than blindly replacing a production configuration.

The manifest subscribes to `team_join`, `user_change`, `member_joined_channel` and
`member_left_channel`, which the membership controller handles. Slack documents
the [member-join](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/team_join/),
[member-change](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/user_change/),
[channel-join](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/member_joined_channel/) and
[channel-leave](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/member_left_channel/) events.
Their required scopes are already in the manifest. A local manifest edit does
not update an installed Slack app.

Invite the app to the intended demo channels. Workspace identity is the admission
boundary: this configuration enables eligible members of that workspace, not just
the operator. Use a dedicated demo workspace.

## Kernel driver and terminal sandbox

The current execution boundary uses macOS Seatbelt. Install Node and the
`agent-browser` package on the trusted host. Kernel hosts Chromium; Browser Use,
local Chromium and requester browser wrappers are not required or permitted.
Python and shell work retain their foreground terminal sandbox.

Inspect the operator commands before preparing the fleet:

```sh
.local/hermes-lab/venv/bin/python scripts/prepare-clanker-execution --help
scripts/enable-clanker-browser --help
```

Prepare with the absolute gateway home, Node executable and installed
agent-browser package directory:

```sh
.local/hermes-lab/venv/bin/python scripts/prepare-clanker-execution \
  --home /ABSOLUTE/GATEWAY/HOME \
  --node /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/node \
  --agent-browser-package /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/agent-browser
```

Preparation installs protected contexts and verifies the primitive terminal
boundary. It does not grant Slack tools. Configure Kernel below, then run
`scripts/enable-clanker-browser --home /ABSOLUTE/GATEWAY/HOME` while the gateway
is fully stopped with zero active agents. Acceptance verifies the current policy,
removes old profile browser wrappers, stops owned legacy local browser processes
and activates Kernel-only tools. It never restarts the gateway.

The launcher restores the public-web terminal egress broker when the fleet
exists. Missing or unaccepted policy must leave browser execution unavailable.
The [earlier execution decision](decisions/2026-10-05-local-execution-boundary.md)
is historical evidence; its local-browser flow is no longer supported.

## Hosted vault

After the gateway has created `slack_membership.json`, expose its loopback vault
service through HTTPS. Register `https://YOUR_VAULT_HOST/auth/callback` in the
Slack app's Sign in with Slack redirect configuration, then run interactively:

```sh
scripts/configure-clanker-vault \
  --public-url https://YOUR_VAULT_HOST \
  --client-id YOUR_SLACK_APP_CLIENT_ID
```

Use the app's numeric client ID. The script prompts privately for the client
secret if it is absent. It writes configuration for loopback port `8767` by
default; it does not deploy the HTTPS proxy or restart the gateway. Run the proxy
and gateway, then verify the public `/health` endpoint, Slack OIDC callback and an
owner-bound access request.

A temporary tunnel's hostname can change. Keep the registered callback and local
vault origin synchronized; links already sent to Slack retain their old URLs.

## Kernel browser

Use the operator's Kernel account. Enter `KERNEL_API_KEY` privately into a mode-600
local `.env`; never paste it in Slack or commit it. Obtain and review the pinned
plugin source documented in [Kernel integration](KERNEL_BROWSER.md). Clanker
loads that provider from protected backend storage, without enabling a raw
Kernel plugin in member profiles or copying its key there.

With Slack membership, hosted vault and the prepared fleet present, preview:

```sh
scripts/configure-clanker-kernel-browser \
  --home /ABSOLUTE/GATEWAY/HOME \
  --plugin-source /ABSOLUTE/REVIEWED/KERNEL/PLUGIN \
  --key-env /ABSOLUTE/PRIVATE/KEY/.env
```

After reviewing the preview, stop the gateway completely and repeat with
`--apply`. Accept the current execution fleet using `enable-clanker-browser`
before starting the gateway. Configuration snapshots contain private data and
must remain in protected ignored storage.

Optional India residential routing uses
`scripts/configure-kernel-residential-proxy --home /ABSOLUTE/GATEWAY/HOME`.
It previews first; `--apply` requires the managed-proxy entitlement and stopped
gateway. Existing browsers with a different routing policy are blocked from
control and private fills. Stop and reopen them within the same task to use the
current policy; a fresh Slack thread is not required. A healthy proxy does not
prove a retailer allows checkout.

Kernel receives website content and entered login secrets. See
[access management](ACCESS_MANAGEMENT.md) for requester binding, deletion checks
and provider trust limits. All shopping, login and personal-detail forms stay in
the same Kernel browser. Automatic payment is unavailable: verify the cart and
give the owner the checkout step, stopping before purchase commitment. There is
no local or alternate browser fallback.

## Start and check

```sh
scripts/hermes-lab gateway run -v
```

Keep that foreground process open. In a second terminal:


"""Requester-owned Kernel sessions behind Hermes's native browser tools."""
import base64
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import time
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit

from vault.store import AccessError
from .service import BrowserContext
from .kernel_client import register_provider, valid_session_record, validate_profile_attachment, validate_proxy_policy, validate_vault_attachments


class KernelBrowser(BrowserContext):
    uses_native_tools = True
    profile_retained_on_stop = False

    def state(self, turn):
        key = self.context_key(turn)
        path = self.directory / 'kernel' / 'contexts' / (key + '.json')
        return path, self.owned_state(turn, path)

    def driver(self, turn):
        from seatbelt.context import Context
        return Context(turn.home).settings['agent_browser_executable']

    def native_task_id(self, turn):
        value = ':'.join((turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id, str(turn.home.resolve()), turn.task_id))
        return 'ck-' + hashlib.sha256(value.encode()).hexdigest()[:40]

    def check_claim(self, turn, session_id):
        with self.vault.store.connection() as db:
            owner = db.execute('SELECT team,requester,context FROM browser_session_owners WHERE provider=? AND session_id=?',
                ('KernelBrowser', session_id)).fetchone()
        expected = (turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id, self.context_key(turn))
        if not owner or tuple(owner) != expected:
            raise AccessError('This Kernel browser has no verified requester ownership.', 403)

    def endpoint_identity(self, cdp_url, session_id):
        try:
            url = urlsplit(cdp_url)
            query = parse_qs(url.query, strict_parsing=True)
            if (url.scheme != 'wss' or url.username or url.password or url.fragment or
                    not (url.hostname or '').endswith(('.kernel.sh', '.onkernel.com')) or
                    url.path != '/browser/cdp' or set(query) != {'jwt'} or len(query['jwt']) != 1):
                raise ValueError
            encoded = query['jwt'][0].split('.')[1]
            payload = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(encoded + '=' * (-len(encoded) % 4)))
            browser = payload['session']
            checks = {'session ID': browser['id'] == session_id,
                'instance hostname': isinstance(browser['fqdn'], str),
                'instance ID': isinstance(browser['instanceUuid'], str) and bool(browser['instanceUuid']),
                # Zero selects Kernel's default CDP port; an empty WebSocket
                # path similarly selects its browser endpoint.
                'CDP port': isinstance(browser['cdpPort'], int) and 0 <= browser['cdpPort'] < 65536,
                'CDP path': isinstance(browser['cdpWsPath'], str)}
            for field, valid in checks.items():
                if not valid:
                    raise AccessError('Kernel returned an unsupported browser control ' + field + '.', 403)
            # These URLs originate in authenticated Kernel API responses. The
            # decoded fields compare their stable routing identity; this is not
            # signature verification or an independent source of authorization.
            return (browser['id'], browser['instanceUuid'], browser['cdpPort'], browser['cdpWsPath'], browser['fqdn'])
        except (ValueError, KeyError, IndexError, TypeError):
            raise AccessError('Kernel returned an unsupported browser control identity.', 403) from None

    def claim_endpoint(self, turn, cdp_url, session_id):
        owner = (turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id, self.context_key(turn))
        identity = self.endpoint_identity(cdp_url, session_id)
        # A different API session ID must not allow two owners to attach to
        # the same underlying browser instance and CDP target.
        endpoint = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(identity[1:]).encode()).hexdigest()
        with self.vault.store.connection() as db:
            db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            row = db.execute('SELECT team,requester,context FROM browser_session_owners WHERE provider=? AND session_id=?',
                ('KernelCDP', endpoint)).fetchone()
            if row and tuple(row) != owner:
                raise AccessError('Kernel returned a brow…1423 tokens truncated…ng could not be verified.', 403)
        if modern_id and legacy_id and modern_id != legacy_id:
            raise AccessError('Kernel browser proxy routing could not be verified.', 403)
        network = remote.get('network')
        if network is not None and not isinstance(network, dict):
            raise AccessError('Kernel browser proxy routing could not be verified.', 403)
        if ((network or {}).get('proxy_routes') or remote.get('bypass_hosts') or
                (proxy or {}).get('bypass_hosts')):
            raise AccessError('Kernel browser has unexpected proxy routing.', 403)
        if policy is None:
            # Default egress is permitted only while the protected policy also
            # selects it. Policy changes require a newly verified browser.
            if modern_id or legacy_id or (proxy is not None and proxy.get('mode') != 'default'):
                raise AccessError('This existing Kernel browser changed its proxy routing.', 403)
        else:
            if (modern_id or legacy_id) != policy['id'] or (proxy is not None and proxy.get('mode') is not None):
                raise AccessError('Kernel browser does not use its captured proxy policy.', 403)
            self.client.verify_proxy(policy)
        return remote if details else True

    def capability_expires_soon(self, cdp_url):
        encoded = parse_qs(urlsplit(cdp_url).query)['jwt'][0].split('.')[1]
        payload = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(encoded + '=' * (-len(encoded) % 4)))
        expires = payload.get('exp')
        return isinstance(expires, (int, float)) and expires <= time.time() + 60

    def native_record(self, turn, entry):
        task_id = self.native_task_id(turn)
        return {'session_name': entry['session_name'], 'bb_session_id': entry['session_id'],
            'cdp_url': entry['cdp_url'], 'features': entry['features'],
            'session_key': task_id, 'owner_task_id': task_id}

    @staticmethod
    def pending_creation_error(entry, message):
        reference = entry.get('diagnostic_ref')
        if isinstance(reference, str) and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{32}', reference):
            message += ' Reference: ' + reference + '.'
        return AccessError(message, 409)

    def prepare(self, turn):
        from tools import browser_tool as native
        from tools.browser_tool_cdp import _ensure_cdp_supervisor
        task_id = self.native_task_id(turn)
        with self.vault.lock_for(turn.home):
            path, state = self.state(turn)
            name = hashlib.sha256(self.thread(turn).encode()).hexdigest()[:24]
            entry = state['sessions'].setdefault(name, {})
            self.check_access(turn, entry)
            if entry.get('dispatch_unknown'):
                raise self.pending_creation_error(entry,
                    'A Kernel creation was not acknowledged. Reconcile it before another browser.')
            profile = self.browser_binding(turn)
            vault = self.browser_vault(turn)
            if entry.get('session_id'):
                self.check_claim(turn, entry['session_id'])
                if self.validate_auth_binding(entry.get('profile_binding')) != profile:
                    # Authentication uses a separate Kernel-owned browser. An
                    # account change gets a fresh automation browser, never an
                    # in-place profile load or copied cookie state.
                    self.close_entry(path, state, name, cleanup_auth=False)
                    entry = state['sessions'].setdefault(name, {})
                remote = self.check_remote(entry, details=True, vault=vault, profile=profile) if entry.get('session_id') else None
                if not remote:
                    self.detach(entry)
                    entry.clear()
            if not entry.get('session_id'):
                policy = validate_proxy_policy(self.settings['proxy']) if 'proxy' in self.settings else None
                entry.update(dispatch_unknown=True, home=str(turn.home.resolve()), proxy_policy=policy,
                    vault_binding=vault, profile_binding=profile)
                state['threads'][self.thread(turn)] = name
                self.save(path, state)
                try:
                    options = {}
                    if vault is not None:
                        options['vault'] = vault
                    if profile is not None:
                        options['profile'] = validate_profile_attachment(
                            {'name': profile['profile_name'], 'save_changes': False})
                    created = self.client.create_session('clanker-' + name, **options)
                except AccessError as error:
                    # An API timeout can occur after creation; preserve the
                    # dispatch marker rather than automatically duplicating it.
                    if getattr(error, 'browser_dispatch_attempted', None) is False:
                        # Proxy validation failed before a browser POST. This
                        # is a known non-dispatch, so a later turn may retry.
                        entry.clear()
                        state['threads'].pop(self.thread(turn), None)
                        self.save(path, state)
                        raise
                    reference = getattr(error, 'diagnostic_ref', None)
                    if isinstance(reference, str) and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{32}', reference):
                        entry['diagnostic_ref'] = reference
                        self.save(path, state)
                    raise
                if not valid_session_record(created):
                    raise AccessError('Kernel did not confirm a browser session.', 502)
                session_id = created['bb_session_id']
                self.claim_session(turn, session_id)
                entry.update(session_id=session_id, cdp_url=created.get('cdp_url'),
                    session_name=created.get('session_name'), features=created.get('features') or {},
                    created_at=time.time(), dispatch_unknown=False)
                self.save(path, state)
                remote = self.check_remote(entry, details=True, vault=vault, profile=profile)
                if not remote:
                    raise AccessError('The newly created Kernel browser is unavailable.', 503)
            self.claim_endpoint(turn, entry['cdp_url'], entry['session_id'])
            state['threads'][self.thread(turn)] = name
            previous_task = entry.get('native_task_id')
            if previous_task and previous_task != task_id:
                self.detach(entry)
            entry.update(native_task_id=task_id, home=str(turn.home.resolve()), last_used=time.time())
            with native._cleanup_lock:
                existing = native._active_sessions.get(task_id)
                if existing and (existing.get('bb_session_id') != entry['session_id'] or
                        existing.get('cdp_url') != entry['cdp_url'] or
                        existing.get('session_key') != task_id or
                        existing.get('owner_task_id') != task_id or
                        existing.get('fallback_from_cloud') or
                        native._session_owner_homes.get(task_id) != str(turn.home.resolve())):
                    raise AccessError('This native browser task is already bound to another browser.', 403)
                refresh = not existing or self.capability_expires_soon(entry['cdp_url'])
                expected_binding = dict(existing) if existing is not None else None
            # detach acquires Hermes's non-reentrant cleanup lock itself. Keep
            # the authenticated owner/home lock while refreshing its capability.
            if refresh and remote['cdp_ws_url'] != entry['cdp_url']:
                self.detach(entry)
                entry['cdp_url'] = remote['cdp_ws_url']
            with native._cleanup_lock:
                replacement = native._active_sessions.get(task_id)
                if replacement is not None and (replacement != expected_binding or
                        native._session_owner_homes.get(task_id) != str(turn.home.resolve())):
                    raise AccessError('The browser binding changed during renewal. Reopen it before proceeding.', 409)
                record = self.native_record(turn, entry)
                native._active_sessions[task_id] = record
                native._session_owner_homes[task_id] = str(turn.home.resolve())
                native._suspect_browser_sessions.pop(task_id, None)
                native._last_active_session_key[task_id] = task_id
                native._cached_agent_browser = self.driver(turn)
                native._agent_browser_resolved = True
            self.save(path, state)
            self.register_redactions(turn, entry)
            _ensure_cdp_supervisor(task_id)
            from tools.browser_supervisor import SUPERVISOR_REGISTRY
            self.assert_supervisor(turn, SUPERVISOR_REGISTRY.get(task_id))
            return record

    def assert_supervisor(self, turn, supervisor):
        from tools import browser_tool as native
        task_id = self.native_task_id(turn)
        if supervisor is None:
            raise AccessError('Open this requester task\'s Kernel browser before using saved access.', 409)
        with self.vault.lock_for(turn.home):
            path, state = self.state(turn)
            _, entry = self.selected(turn, state)
            self.check_access(turn, entry)
            self.check_claim(turn, entry['session_id'])
            record = native._active_sessions.get(task_id) or {}
            if (entry.get('native_task_id') != task_id or
                    entry.get('home') != str(turn.home.resolve()) or
                    native._session_owner_homes.get(task_id) != str(turn.home.resolve()) or
                    record.get('session_key') != task_id or record.get('owner_task_id') != task_id or
                    record.get('bb_session_id') != entry['session_id'] or
                    record.get('cdp_url') != entry['cdp_url'] or
                    supervisor.cdp_url != entry['cdp_url'] or record.get('fallback_from_cloud')):
                raise AccessError('The browser control endpoint does not belong to this requester task.', 403)
            if not self.check_remote(entry, vault=self.browser_vault(turn), profile=self.browser_binding(turn)):
                raise AccessError('The Kernel browser has expired. Reopen it before using saved access.', 409)
            self.register_redactions(turn, entry)
            return supervisor

    def register_redactions(self, turn, entry):
        kernel = getattr(self.vault, 'kernel_vault', None)
        if kernel is None:
            raise AccessError('Kernel Vault is required for private browser observation.', 503)
        kernel.register_values(turn)
        self.vault.personal.register_redactions(turn)

    def remember_redactions(self, turn, values):
        kernel = getattr(self.vault, 'kernel_vault', None)
        if kernel is None:
            raise AccessError('Kernel Vault is required for private browser observation.', 503)
        from tools.browser_supervisor import SUPERVISOR_REGISTRY
        supervisor = SUPERVISOR_REGISTRY.get(self.native_task_id(turn))
        self.assert_supervisor(turn, supervisor)
        kernel.remember_values(turn, values)

    def finish(self, turn, result):
        kernel = getattr(self.vault, 'kernel_vault', None)
        if kernel is None:
            raise AccessError('Kernel Vault is required for private browser observation.', 503)
        from tools.browser_supervisor import SUPERVISOR_REGISTRY
        self.assert_supervisor(turn, SUPERVISOR_REGISTRY.get(self.native_task_id(turn)))
        kernel.refresh_privacy(turn)
        from agent.redact import redact_registered_vault_values, redact_sensitive_text
        from agent.vault_store import scrub_secret_from_text
        values = kernel.observation_values(turn)
        def scrub(value, key=None):
            if isinstance(value, str):
                # Native image payloads must remain valid for Hermes's image
                # attachment path. Text and metadata still pass the same scrub.
                if value.startswith('data:image/'):
                    return value
                for secret in sorted(values, key=len, reverse=True):
                    value = (value.replace(secret, '«redacted-vault-secret»') if len(secret) == 1
                             else scrub_secret_from_text(value, {'value': secret}))
                return redact_registered_vault_values(redact_sensitive_text(value, force=True))
            if isinstance(value, dict):
                return {scrub(key): scrub(item, key) for key, item in value.items()}
            if isinstance(value, list):
                return [scrub(item) for item in value]
            if type(value) in (int, float) and str(value) in values:
                return '«redacted-vault-secret»'
            return value
        if isinstance(result, dict) and result.get('_multimodal'):
            return scrub(result)
        if isinstance(result, str):
            try:
                parsed = json.loads(result)
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                return scrub(result)
            return json.dumps(scrub(parsed))
        return json.dumps(scrub(result))

    def detach(self, entry):
        from tools import browser_tool as native
        from tools.browser_tool_cdp import _stop_cdp_supervisor
        from tools.browser_supervisor import SUPERVISOR_REGISTRY
        from tools.browser_tool_lifecycle import _kill_verified_daemon
        import os
        import shutil
        task_id = entry.get('native_task_id')
        if not task_id:
            return
        # Only remove a process-local binding that still names our exact CDP
        # endpoint. Local checkout supervision may have replaced it.
        with native._cleanup_lock:
            record = native._active_sessions.get(task_id) or {}
            if record.get('bb_session_id') == entry.get('session_id') and record.get('cdp_url') == entry.get('cdp_url'):
                supervisor = SUPERVISOR_REGISTRY.get(task_id)
                if supervisor is not None and supervisor.cdp_url == entry.get('cdp_url'):
                    _stop_cdp_supervisor(task_id)
                socket_dir = os.path.join(native._socket_safe_tmpdir(), 'agent-browser-' + entry['session_name'])
                if os.path.isdir(socket_dir) and _kill_verified_daemon(socket_dir, entry['session_name']):
                    shutil.rmtree(socket_dir, ignore_errors=True)
                native._active_sessions.pop(task_id, None)
                native._session_owner_homes.pop(task_id, None)
                native._last_active_session_key.pop(task_id, None)
                native._session_last_activity.pop(task_id, None)

    def close_entry(self, path, state, name, *, cleanup_auth=True):
        entry = state['sessions'][name]
        threads = [key for key, value in state['threads'].items() if value == name]
        if entry.get('dispatch_unknown'):
            raise self.pending_creation_error(entry,
                'A Kernel creation needs reconciliation before cleanup can be confirmed.')
        if entry.get('session_id'):
            with self.vault.store.connection() as db:
                claim = db.execute('SELECT team,requester,context FROM browser_session_owners WHERE provider=? AND session_id=?',
                    ('KernelBrowser', entry['session_id'])).fetchone()
            owner = state['owner']
            if not claim or tuple(claim) != (owner['team'], owner['requester'], path.stem):
                raise AccessError('Kernel cleanup is not authorized for this browser owner.', 403)
        if entry.get('session_id') and not self.client.close_verified(entry['session_id']):
            entry['cleanup_pending'] = True
            self.save(path, state)
            raise AccessError('Kernel browser deletion could not be verified. This account remains blocked.', 503)
        self.detach(entry)
        state['sessions'].pop(name)
        state['threads'] = {key: value for key, value in state['threads'].items() if value != name}
        self.save(path, state)
        manager = getattr(self.vault, 'kernel_auth', None)
        if cleanup_auth and manager is not None:
            owner = state['owner']
            for thread in threads or [None]:
                manager.cleanup_context(owner['team'], owner['requester'], entry['home'], thread=thread)

    def stop(self, turn, session=None, *, purge=False):
        if session is not None:
            raise AccessError('Kernel browser selection belongs to the authenticated thread.', 403)
        with self.vault.lock_for(turn.home):
            path, state = self.state(turn)
            names = list(state['sessions']) if purge else [state['threads'].get(self.thread(turn))]
            errors = []
            for name in names:
                if name not in state['sessions']:
                    continue
                try:
                    entry = state['sessions'][name]
                    if entry.get('session_id'):
                        self.check_claim(turn, entry['session_id'])
                    self.close_entry(path, state, name, cleanup_auth=False)
                except AccessError as error:
                    errors.append(error)
            if errors:
                raise errors[0]
            manager = getattr(self.vault, 'kernel_auth', None)
            if manager is not None:
                manager.cleanup_context(turn.source.scope_id, turn.source.user_id,
                    str(turn.home.resolve()), thread=None if purge else self.thread(turn))

    def stop_by_home(self, home):

                        except AccessError as error:
                            errors.append(error)
            if errors:
                raise errors[0]
            manager = getattr(self.vault, 'kernel_auth', None)
            if manager is not None:

"""Hosted form and Slack OIDC. No credential bodies or access URLs are logged."""
import asyncio
import hmac
import json
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlencode, urlsplit

from aiohttp import web, ClientSession, ClientTimeout
import jwt

from .store import AccessError

SECURITY_HEADERS = {
    'Cache-Control':'no-store', 'Referrer-Policy':'no-referrer',
    'X-Content-Type-Options':'nosniff', 'X-Frame-Options':'DENY',
    'Content-Security-Policy':"default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'",
}


def verify_slack_token(token, key, audience, nonce):
    try:
        claims = jwt.decode(token,key,algorithms=['RS256'],audience=audience,
                            issuer='https://slack.com',options={'require':['exp','iat','iss','aud','nonce','sub']})
        if not hmac.compare_digest(str(claims['nonce']),nonce):
            raise ValueError('nonce')
        identity={'team':claims['https://slack.com/team_id'],'owner':claims['https://slack.com/user_id']}
        if not all(isinstance(value,str) and value for value in identity.values()):
            raise ValueError('identity')
        return identity
    except (jwt.PyJWTError,ValueError,KeyError):
        raise AccessError('Slack sign-in could not be verified.',403) from None


class VaultWeb:
    def __init__(self, service, config, *, verify_identity=None):
        self.service, self.store, self.config = service, service.store, config
        self.origin = config['public_url'].rstrip('/')
        parts = urlsplit(self.origin)
        if parts.scheme != 'https' and not config.get('local_test'):
            raise ValueError('The hosted credential form requires HTTPS')
        if parts.path not in ('','/') or parts.query or parts.fragment or parts.username or not parts.hostname:
            raise ValueError('public_url must be a website origin')
        self.verify_identity = verify_identity or self.slack_identity
        self.app = web.Application(client_max_size=16384, middlewares=[self.errors])
        self.app.router.add_get('/vault/fill',self.page)
        self.app.router.add_get('/vault',self.page)
        self.app.router.add_get('/assets/vault.js',self.asset)
        self.app.router.add_get('/assets/vault.css',self.asset)
        self.app.router.add_get('/auth/callback',self.callback)
        self.app.router.add_get('/health',self.health)
        self.app.router.add_post('/auth/start',self.auth_start)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/request',self.request)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/items',self.items)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/personal/details',self.personal_details)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/personal/remove',self.personal_remove)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/disconnect',self.disconnect)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/invitations',self.invitations)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/invite',self.invite)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/invite/revoke',self.revoke_invitation)

    @web.middleware
    async def errors(self, request, handler):
        try:
            if request.method=='POST' and request.headers.get('Origin')!=self.origin:
                raise AccessError('This request did not come from the credential form.', 403)
            response = await handler(request)
        except AccessError as exc:
            response = web.json_response({'error':str(exc)},status=exc.status)
        except (ValueError,KeyError,TypeError,json.JSONDecodeError):
            response = web.json_response({'error':'The request is invalid.'},status=400)
        except web.HTTPException as exc:
            response = web.Response(body=exc.body,status=exc.status,headers=exc.headers)
        except Exception:
            # Never echo exception bodies: a vault/provider exception may contain input.
            response = web.json_response({'error':'Could not complete this operation. Your task is still saved.'},status=503)
        response.headers.update(SECURITY_HEADERS)
        if not self.config.get('local_test'):
            response.headers['Strict-Transport-Security']='max-age=31536000'
        return response

    async def health(self, request):
        return web.json_response({'ready':True})

    async def page(self, request):
        return web.Response(text=Path(__file__).with_name('page.html').read_text(),content_type='text/html')

class AccessError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, status=400):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status


def digest(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(value.encode()).hexdigest()


class RequestStore:
    def __init__(self, directory, *, clock=time.time):
        self.directory = Path(directory)
        self.directory.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        os.chmod(self.directory, 0o700)
        self.clock = clock
        key = self.directory / 'request.key'
        if not key.exists():
            fd = os.open(key, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
            with os.fdopen(fd, 'wb') as stream:
                stream.write(secrets.token_bytes(32))
                stream.flush()
                os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        self.key = key.read_bytes()
        self.path = self.directory / 'requests.sqlite'
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.executescript('''
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS requests (
                  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, team TEXT NOT NULL, owner TEXT NOT NULL,
                  home TEXT NOT NULL, task_id TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL,
                  task TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, label TEXT NOT NULL,
                  origin TEXT NOT NULL, identifier TEXT NOT NULL,
                  created REAL NOT NULL, expires REAL NOT NULL,
                  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'waiting', handle TEXT,
                  message_ts TEXT, resume_attempt REAL, resume_delivered REAL);
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_states (
                  state TEXT PRIMARY KEY, browser TEXT NOT NULL, nonce TEXT NOT NULL,
                  request_id TEXT NOT NULL, expires REAL NOT NULL);
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
                  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, team TEXT NOT NULL, owner TEXT NOT NULL,
                  csrf TEXT NOT NULL, expires REAL NOT NULL);
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS transfers (
                  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, team TEXT NOT NULL, owner TEXT NOT NULL,
                  home TEXT NOT NULL, task_id TEXT NOT NULL, original_source TEXT NOT NULL,
                  task TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT, created REAL NOT NULL,
                  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'waiting');
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS private_link_deliveries (
                  request_id TEXT NOT NULL, event_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                  message_ts TEXT NOT NULL,
                  PRIMARY KEY(request_id,event_id));
            ''')
            # Hermes reuses a session id across turns. Older development stores
            # made that id unique, dropping every later handoff in the thread.
            transfer_schema = db.execute("SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='transfers'").fetchone()[0]
            if 'UNIQUE(team,owner,task_id)' in transfer_schema.replace(' ', ''):

                      id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, team TEXT NOT NULL, owner TEXT NOT NULL,
                      home TEXT NOT NULL, task_id TEXT NOT NULL, original_source TEXT NOT NULL,
                      task TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT, created REAL NOT NULL,
                      status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'waiting');
                    INSERT INTO transfers SELECT * FROM transfers_legacy;
                    DROP TABLE transfers_legacy;
                    COMMIT;
                ''')
            if 'code_payload' not in {row[1] for row in db.execute('PRAGMA table_info(requests)')}:
                db.execute('ALTER TABLE requests ADD COLUMN code_payload BLOB')
            columns = {row[1] for row in db.execute('PRAGMA table_info(requests)')}
            for name, kind in [('checkout','TEXT'),('payment_payload','BLOB'),('payment_expires','REAL'),

            columns = {row[1] for row in db.execute('PRAGMA table_info(transfers)')}
            for name, kind in [('reply_mode', "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'private'"),

    @contextmanager
    def connection(self):
        db = sqlite3.connect(self.path, timeout=15)
        db.execute('PRAGMA secure_delete=ON')
        db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        try:
            with db:
                yield db
        finally:
            db.close()

    def token(self, request_id):
        return hmac.new(self.key, request_id.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

    def create(self, *, team, owner, home, task_id, source, task, kind, label, origin, identifier='', handle=None, checkout=None, grant_id=None, approver=None, gateway_event_id=None, login_method='password'):
        if kind not in ('login','code','api_key','payment'):
            raise AccessError('This access form supports logins, cards, API keys and verification codes.')
        if login_method not in ('password', 'sms') or (login_method == 'sms' and kind not in ('login', 'code')):
            raise AccessError('Unsupported login method for this request.')
        if login_method == 'sms' and identifier:
            raise AccessError('Phone numbers must be supplied through the private form.')
        if (kind=='payment') != isinstance(checkout,dict):
            raise AccessError('Card requests require a bound checkout.')
        checkout_json = json.dumps(checkout,sort_keys=True) if checkout is not None else None
        if kind=='api_key':
            from agent.vault_store import VaultError, normalize_origin
            from urllib.parse import urlsplit
            if not isinstance(origin,str):
                raise AccessError('API keys require an exact HTTPS API origin.')
            parts=urlsplit(origin)
            if parts.scheme!='https' or not parts.hostname or parts.path not in ('','/') or parts.query or parts.fragment or parts.username or parts.password:
                raise AccessError('API keys require an exact HTTPS API origin.')
            try:origin=normalize_origin(origin)
            except (VaultError,ValueError):
                raise AccessError('API keys require an exact HTTPS API origin.') from None
            if not isinstance(label,str) or not label.strip() or len(label)>120 or identifier or handle:
                raise AccessError('API key requests require a title and no login fields.')
            label=label.strip()
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            row = db.execute("SELECT * FROM requests WHERE team=? AND owner=? AND task_id=? AND task=? AND origin=? AND kind=? AND identifier=? AND handle IS ? AND checkout IS ? AND grant_id IS ? AND approver IS ? AND gateway_event_id IS ? AND login_method=? AND status='waiting' AND expires>?",
                             (team, owner, task_id, task, origin, kind, identifier, handle, checkout_json, grant_id, approver, gateway_event_id, login_method, self.clock())).fetchone()
            if row:
                return dict(row)
            request_id = secrets.token_hex(16)
            now = self.clock()
            db.execute('INSERT INTO requests (id,team,owner,home,task_id,source,task,kind,label,origin,identifier,created,expires,handle,checkout,grant_id,approver,gateway_event_id,login_method) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)',
                       (request_id,team,owner,str(home),task_id,json.dumps(source),task,kind,label,origin,identifier,now,now+({'code':300,'payment':900}.get(kind,1800)),handle,checkout_json,grant_id,approver,gateway_event_id,login_method))
            return dict(db.execute('SELECT * FROM requests WHERE id=?', (request_id,)).fetchone())

    def get(self, request_id, token, *, identity=None, waiting=True):
        if not isinstance(token, str) or not hmac.compare_digest(self.token(request_id), token):
            raise AccessError('This access link is invalid.', 404)
        with self.connection() as db:
            row = db.execute('SELECT * FROM requests WHERE id=?', (request_id,)).fetchone()
        if not row:
            raise AccessError('This access link is invalid.', 404)
        row = dict(row)
        if identity and (row['team'],row.get('approver') or row['owner']) != (identity['team'],identity['owner']):
            raise AccessError('Sign in with the Slack account that requested this task.', 403)
        if row['expires'] <= self.clock():
            raise AccessError('This access link has expired. Ask Clanker for a new link.', 410)
        if waiting and row['status'] != 'waiting':
            raise AccessError('This access link has already been used or cancelled.', 410)
        return row

    def start_auth(self, request_id):
        state, browser, nonce = (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) for _ in range(3))
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.execute('DELETE FROM auth_states WHERE expires<=?', (self.clock(),))
            db.execute('INSERT INTO auth_states VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)',
                       (digest(state),digest(browser),nonce,request_id,self.clock()+600))
        return state, browser, nonce

    def consume_auth(self, state, browser):
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            row = db.execute('SELECT * FROM auth_states WHERE state=?', (digest(state),)).fetchone()
            if not row or row['expires'] <= self.clock() or not hmac.compare_digest(row['browser'],digest(browser)):
                raise AccessError('Sign-in expired or could not be verified. Open your access link again.', 403)
            db.execute('DELETE FROM auth_states WHERE state=?', (digest(state),))
            return dict(row)

    def new_session(self, team, owner):
        sid, csrf = secrets.token_urlsafe(32), secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.execute('DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expires<=?', (self.clock(),))
            db.execute('INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)', (digest(sid),team,owner,csrf,self.clock()+3600))
        return sid

    def session(self, sid):
        with self.connection() as db:
            row = db.execute('SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE id=? AND expires>?', (digest(sid),self.clock())).fetchone()
        if not row:
            raise AccessError('Sign in with Slack to continue.', 401)
        return dict(row)

  const timer=controller?setTimeout(()=>controller.abort(),20000):null;
  try{
    const response = await fetch(path,{method:'POST',credentials:'same-origin',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json','X-CSRF-Token':csrf},body:JSON.stringify(data),...(controller?{signal:controller.signal}:{})});
    const result = await response.json();

  let url;

    ?authHosts.includes(url.hostname)&&url.pathname.startsWith('/login/')&&url.pathname.length>7&&!url.hash

  if(url.protocol!=='https:'||!allowed||url.port||url.username||url.password)

"""Hosted form and Slack OIDC. No credential bodies or access URLs are logged."""
import asyncio
import hmac
import json
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlencode, urlsplit

from aiohttp import web, ClientSession, ClientTimeout
import jwt

from .store import AccessError

SECURITY_HEADERS = {
    'Cache-Control':'no-store', 'Referrer-Policy':'no-referrer',
    'X-Content-Type-Options':'nosniff', 'X-Frame-Options':'DENY',
    'Content-Security-Policy':"default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'",
}


def verify_slack_token(token, key, audience, nonce):
    try:
        claims = jwt.decode(token,key,algorithms=['RS256'],audience=audience,
                            issuer='https://slack.com',options={'require':['exp','iat','iss','aud','nonce','sub']})
        if not hmac.compare_digest(str(claims['nonce']),nonce):
            raise ValueError('nonce')
        identity={'team':claims['https://slack.com/team_id'],'owner':claims['https://slack.com/user_id']}
        if not all(isinstance(value,str) and value for value in identity.values()):
            raise ValueError('identity')
        return identity
    except (jwt.PyJWTError,ValueError,KeyError):
        raise AccessError('Slack sign-in could not be verified.',403) from None


class VaultWeb:
    def __init__(self, service, config, *, verify_identity=None):
        self.service, self.store, self.config = service, service.store, config
        self.origin = config['public_url'].rstrip('/')
        parts = urlsplit(self.origin)
        if parts.scheme != 'https' and not config.get('local_test'):
            raise ValueError('The hosted credential form requires HTTPS')
        if parts.path not in ('','/') or parts.query or parts.fragment or parts.username or not parts.hostname:
            raise ValueError('public_url must be a website origin')
        self.verify_identity = verify_identity or self.slack_identity
        self.app = web.Application(client_max_size=16384, middlewares=[self.errors])
        self.app.router.add_get('/vault/fill',self.page)
        self.app.router.add_get('/vault',self.page)
        self.app.router.add_get('/assets/vault.js',self.asset)
        self.app.router.add_get('/assets/vault.css',self.asset)
        self.app.router.add_get('/auth/callback',self.callback)
        self.app.router.add_get('/health',self.health)
        self.app.router.add_post('/auth/start',self.auth_start)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/request',self.request)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/items',self.items)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/personal/details',self.personal_details)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/personal/remove',self.personal_remove)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/disconnect',self.disconnect)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/invitations',self.invitations)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/invite',self.invite)
        self.app.router.add_post('/api/invite/revoke',self.revoke_invitation)

    @web.middleware
    async def errors(self, request, handler):
        try:
            if request.method=='POST' and request.headers.get('Origin')!=self.origin:
                raise AccessError('This request did not come from the credential form.', 403)
            response = await handler(request)
        except AccessError as exc:
            response = web.json_response({'error':str(exc)},status=exc.status)
        except (ValueError,KeyError,TypeError,json.JSONDecodeError):
            response = web.json_response({'error':'The request is invalid.'},status=400)
        except web.HTTPException as exc:
            response = web.Response(body=exc.body,status=exc.status,headers=exc.headers)
        except Exception:
            # Never echo exception bodies: a vault/provider exception may contain input.
            response = web.json_response({'error':'Could not complete this operation. Your task is still saved.'},status=503)
        response.headers.update(SECURITY_HEADERS)
        if not self.config.get('local_test'):
            response.headers['Strict-Transport-Security']='max-age=31536000'
        return response

    async def health(self, request):
        return web.json_response({'ready':True})

    async def page(self, request):
        return web.Response(text=Path(__file__).with_name('page.html').read_text(),content_type='text/html')

    async def asset(self, request):
        name = request.path.rsplit('/',1)[-1]
        return web.Response(text=Path(__file__).with_name(name).read_text(),content_type='text/javascript' if name.endswith('.js') else 'text/css')

    def identity(self, request, *, csrf=False):
        identity = self.store.session(request.cookies.get('__Host-clanker',''))
        self.service.validate_member(identity['team'],identity['owner'])
        if csrf and not hmac.compare_digest(request.headers.get('X-CSRF-Token',''),identity['csrf']):
            raise AccessError('The form session could not be verified. Reload the page.',403)
        return identity

    async def auth_start(self, request):
        data = await request.json()
        row = self.store.get(data['id'],data['token']) if data else None
        if row:self.service.validate_member(row['team'],row['owner'])
        state,browser,nonce = self.store.start_auth(row['id'] if row else '')
        query = urlencode({'response_type':'code','scope':'openid profile','client_id':self.config['client_id'],
                           'state':state,'nonce':nonce,'team':row['team'] if row else self.service.policy.team,
                           'redirect_uri':self.origin+'/auth/callback'})
        response = web.json_response({'url':'https://slack.com/openid/connect/authorize?'+query})
        response.set_cookie('__Host-clanker-auth',browser,secure=True,httponly=True,samesite='Lax',max_age=600,path='/')
        return response

    async def slack_identity(self, code, nonce):
        from agent.secret_scope import build_profile_secret_scope
        secret = build_profile_secret_scope(self.service.policy.home).get('CLANKER_SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET')
        if not secret:
            raise AccessError('Slack sign-in has not been configured.',503)
        async with ClientSession(timeout=ClientTimeout(total=15)) as client:
            async with client.post('https://slack.com/api/openid.connect.token',data={
                'client_id':self.config['client_id'],'client_secret':secret,'code':code,
                'redirect_uri':self.origin+'/auth/callback'}) as response:
                result = await response.json()
        if not result.get('ok') or not result.get('id_token'):
            raise AccessError('Slack could not verify this sign-in. Open your access link again.',403)
        def decode():
            key = jwt.PyJWKClient('https://slack.com/openid/connect/keys',timeout=10).get_signing_key_from_jwt(result['id_token'])
            return verify_slack_token(result['id_token'],key.key,self.config['client_id'],nonce)
        return await asyncio.to_thread(decode)

    async def callback(self, request):
        auth = self.store.consume_auth(request.query.get('state',''),request.cookies.get('__Host-clanker-auth',''))

            # Hermes reuses a session id across turns. Older development stores

        if kind not in ('login','code','api_key','payment'):
            raise AccessError('This access form supports logins, cards, API keys and verification codes.')

            db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            row = db.execute("SELECT * FROM requests WHERE team=? AND owner=? AND task_id=? AND task=? AND origin=? AND kind=? AND identifier=? AND handle IS ? AND checkout IS ? AND grant_id IS ? AND approver IS ? AND gateway_event_id IS ? AND login_method=? AND status='waiting' AND expires>?",
                             (team, owner, task_id, task, origin, kind, identifier, handle, checkout_json, grant_id, approver, gateway_event_id, login_method, self.clock())).fetchone()
            if row:
                return dict(row)
            request_id = secrets.token_hex(16)

            db.execute('INSERT INTO requests (id,team,owner,home,task_id,source,task,kind,label,origin,identifier,created,expires,handle,checkout,grant_id,approver,gateway_event_id,login_method) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)',
                       (request_id,team,owner,str(home),task_id,json.dumps(source),task,kind,label,origin,identifier,now,now+({'code':300,'payment':900}.get(kind,1800)),handle,checkout_json,grant_id,approver,gateway_event_id,login_method))
            return dict(db.execute('SELECT * FROM requests WHERE id=?', (request_id,)).fetchone())

    def get(self, request_id, token, *, identity=None, waiting=True):
        if not isinstance(token, str) or not hmac.compare_digest(self.token(request_id), token):
            raise AccessError('This access link is invalid.', 404)
        with self.connection() as db:
            row = db.execute('SELECT * FROM requests WHERE id=?', (request_id,)).fetchone()
        if not row:
            raise AccessError('This access link is invalid.', 404)
        row = dict(row)
        if identity and (row['team'],row.get('approver') or row['owner']) != (identity['team'],identity['owner']):
            raise AccessError('Sign in with the Slack account that requested this task.', 403)
        if row['expires'] <= self.clock():
            raise AccessError('This access link has expired. Ask Clanker for a new link.', 410)
        if waiting and row['status'] != 'waiting':
            raise AccessError('This access link has already been used or cancelled.', 410)
        return row

    def start_auth(self, request_id):
        state, browser, nonce = (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) for _ in range(3))
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.execute('DELETE FROM auth_states WHERE expires<=?', (self.clock(),))
            db.execute('INSERT INTO auth_states VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)',
                       (digest(state),digest(browser),nonce,request_id,self.clock()+600))
        return state, browser, nonce

    def consume_auth(self, state, browser):
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
            row = db.execute('SELECT * FROM auth_states WHERE state=?', (digest(state),)).fetchone()
            if not row or row['expires'] <= self.clock() or not hmac.compare_digest(row['browser'],digest(browser)):
                raise AccessError('Sign-in expired or could not be verified. Open your access link again.', 403)
            db.execute('DELETE FROM auth_states WHERE state=?', (digest(state),))
            return dict(row)

    def new_session(self, team, owner):
        sid, csrf = secrets.token_urlsafe(32), secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
        with self.connection() as db:
            db.execute('DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expires<=?', (self.clock(),))
            db.execute('INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)', (digest(sid),team,owner,csrf,self.clock()+3600))
        return sid

    def session(self, sid):
        with self.connection() as db:
            row = db.execute('SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE id=? AND expires>?', (digest(sid),self.clock())).fetchone()
        if not row:
            raise AccessError('Sign in with Slack to continue.', 401)
        return dict(row)

  const controller=['/api/items','/api/invitations'].includes(path)?new AbortController():null;
  const timer=controller?setTimeout(()=>controller.abort(),20000):null;
  try{
    const response = await fetch(path,{method:'POST',credentials:'same-origin',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json','X-CSRF-Token':csrf},body:JSON.stringify(data),...(controller?{signal:controller.signal}:{})});
    const result = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) { const error = new Error(result.error || 'Please try again.');error.status=response.status;throw error; }
    return result;
  }catch(error){
    if(error.name==='AbortError')throw new Error('The connection timed out. Try again to load your accounts.');
    throw error;
  }finally{if(timer!==null)clearTimeout(timer);}

  let url;
  try{url=new URL(result.collection_url);}catch{throw new Error('The secure form is unavailable. Please reopen your access link.');}
  const authHosts=['auth.kernel.com','auth.kernel.sh','auth.onkernel.com','managed-auth.onkernel.com'];

    ?authHosts.includes(url.hostname)&&url.pathname.startsWith('/login/')&&url.pathname.length>7&&!url.hash

  if(url.protocol!=='https:'||!allowed||url.port||url.username||url.password)

  if(replace)location.replace(url.href);else location.assign(url.href);

"""Sanitized operator diagnostics for the protected Kernel API boundary."""
from contextlib import contextmanager
from contextvars import ContextVar
import hashlib
import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path
import re
import time
import traceback
from urllib.parse import quote, quote_plus, urlsplit
import uuid

import requests

from vault.store import AccessError

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
_active = ContextVar('clanker_kernel_diagnostic', default=None)
_URL = re.compile(r'\b(?:https?|wss?)://[^\s<>\"\']+', re.IGNORECASE)
_BEARER = re.compile(r'\bBearer\s+[^\s\"\',;]+', re.IGNORECASE)


def _http_failed(request):
    status = request['upstream_status']
    return status is not None and status >= 300 and not (
        status == 404 and request['method'] in ('GET', 'DELETE'))


def current(client):
    diagnostic = _active.get()
    return diagnostic if diagnostic is not None and diagnostic.client is client else None


@contextmanager
def operation(client, name, task_id=None):
    # Deletion and its verification read form one operation, including its error
    # reference. ContextVars keep concurrent requester operations independent.
    existing = current(client)
    if existing is not None:
        yield existing
        return
    diagnostic = KernelDiagnostic(client, name, task_id)
    token = _active.set(diagnostic)
    try:
        yield diagnostic
    finally:
        _active.reset(token)


class KernelDiagnostic:
    def __init__(self, client, name, task_id):
        self.client = client
        self.reference = uuid.uuid4().hex
        self.secrets = set()
        self.logged = False
        self.event = {'event': 'kernel_upstream_failure', 'provider': 'kernel',
                      'operation': name, 'diagnostic_ref': self.reference, 'requests': []}
        if task_id is not None:
            self.event['task_ref'] = hashlib.sha256(str(task_id).encode()).hexdigest()[:24]

    def remember_secret(self, value):
        if isinstance(value, str) and value:
            self.secrets.update((value, quote(value, safe=''), quote_plus(value),
                                 json.dumps(value)[1:-1]))

    def text(self, value, limit=1000):
        # Sanitize BEFORE constructing a LogRecord: log formatters may run in a
        # different thread, and ordinary profile redaction can be switched off.
        try:
            from agent.redact import redact_sensitive_text
            text = str(value).replace('\\/', '/')
            for secret in sorted(self.secrets, key=len, reverse=True):
                text = text.replace(secret, '[REDACTED]')
            if len(text) > 8192:
                return '[oversized diagnostic text omitted]'
            text = _URL.sub('[REDACTED_URL]', text)
            text = _BEARER.sub('Bearer [REDACTED]', text)
            text = redact_sensitive_text(text, force=True, redact_url_credentials=True)
            return text[:limit]
        except Exception:
            return '[diagnostic text unavailable]'

    def error_fields(self, response):
        # Success records contain control capabilities; never inspect or log
        # them. Error bodies are untrusted: retain only scalar code/message.
        try:
            if len(response.content) > 8192:
                return {'format': 'oversized_body_omitted'}
            body = response.json()
        except Exception:
            return {'format': 'non_json'}
        if not isinstance(body, dict):
            return {'format': 'unsupported_json'}
        fields = {}
        for name in ('code', 'message', 'error'):
            value = body.get(name)
            if isinstance(value, (str, int)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
                fields[name] = self.text(value)
            elif name == 'error' and isinstance(value, dict):
                fields[name] = {key: self.text(value[key]) for key in ('code', 'message')
                               if isinstance(value.get(key), (str, int))}
        return fields

    def request(self, method, url, call, *args, **kwargs):
        authorization = kwargs.get('headers', {}).get('Authorization', '')
        if authorization.startswith('Bearer '):
            self.remember_secret(authorization[7:])
        path = urlsplit(url).path
        route = ('/browsers/{id}' if path.startswith('/browsers/') else
            '/proxies/{id}/check' if re.fullmatch(r'/proxies/[^/]+/check', path) else
            '/proxies/{id}' if re.fullmatch(r'/proxies/[^/]+', path) else
            path if path in ('/browsers', '/proxies') else '[other]')
        event = {'method': method, 'route': route, 'upstream_status': None,
                 'timeout_seconds': kwargs.get('timeout')}
        self.event['requests'].append(event)
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            response = call(url, *args, **kwargs)
            event['upstream_status'] = response.status_code
            for header in ('x-request-id', 'request-id'):
                value = response.headers.get(header)
                if isinstance(value, str) and re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,128}', value):
                    event['provider_request_id'] = self.text(value, 128)
                    break
            expected_absence = response.status_code == 404 and method in ('GET', 'DELETE')
            if response.status_code >= 300 and not expected_absence:
                event['upstream_error'] = self.error_fields(response)
            return response
        except Exception as error:
            event['exception_type'] = type(error).__module__ + '.' + type(error).__name__
            raise
        finally:
            event['elapsed_ms'] = round((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000, 2)

    def failure(self, error=None, kind=None):
        if self.logged:
            return
        chain = []
        seen = set()
        while error is not None and id(error) not in seen and len(chain) < 6:
            seen.add(id(error))
            if kind is None:
                if isinstance(error, requests.Timeout):
                    kind = 'timeout'
                elif isinstance(error, requests.ConnectionError):
                    kind = 'connection_error'
            # A provider HTTP exception can repeat its raw body. The selected
            # HTTP error fields above already preserve the useful detail.
            http_error = any(_http_failed(request) for request in self.event['requests'])
            chain.append({'type': type(error).__module__ + '.' + type(error).__name__,
                          'message': '[see upstream_error]' if http_error else self.text(error),
                          'frames': [{'file': Path(frame.filename).name,
                                      'function': frame.name, 'line': frame.lineno}
                                     for frame in traceback.extract_tb(error.__traceback__)[-8:]]})
            error = error.__cause__ or error.__context__
        if kind is None and any(_http_failed(request) for request in self.event['requests']):
            kind = 'http_error'
        self.event.update(failure_kind=kind or 'provider_exception', exception_chain=chain)
        self.logged = True
        # No exception objects, raw headers/bodies, locals or tracebacks enter
        # the logging queue. json.dumps escapes control characters in messages.
        try:
            logger.warning('Kernel upstream failure %s', json.dumps(self.event, sort_keys=True))
        except Exception:
            pass  # A broken operator log sink must not alter provider outcomes.

    def access_error(self, message, status):
        error = AccessError(message + ' Reference: ' + self.reference + '.', status)
        error.diagnostic_ref = self.reference
        return error
# Kernel Managed Auth migration

Website sign-in now uses one generic Kernel Managed Auth integration. Kernel
owns login discovery, password entry, account choices and interactive SMS/email
verification. There are no merchant-specific selectors, phone rewrites or retry
rules in this migration.

Clanker privately delivers an authenticated owner-only link and carries the
original task context internally. A pending flow is reused; starting another
login would cancel the old Kernel flow. The original task resumes only after the
same owned flow reports `SUCCESS` and its connection reports `AUTHENTICATED`.
Failed or expired flows need a fresh ordinary owner request, without an exact
approval phrase or automatic SMS loop.

Each workspace/requester/account/task has an isolated profile. Automation opens
a fresh browser with the successful snapshot and explicit `save_changes: false`.
Owner membership, invitations, request state and remote profile identity are
checked before attachment. Cancellation, revocation and delayed cleanup cannot
revive a request or delete a replacement flow. Unconfirmed dispatch and cleanup
remain blocked for reconciliation.

Existing Vault login items stay protected. Kernel documents no import bridge
from their write-only fields into Managed Auth credentials, so first sign-in may
require credentials again. Personal details and approved backend API-key
execution continue through Kernel Vault.

## Verification

- Canonical runner: 22 scoped files, **769 passed, 0 failed**, frozen source
  unchanged. The first run caught a compatibility schema regression; the final
  run preserves the declarative, value-free legacy alias schema.
- Real disposable Kernel checks verified hosted login creation, HTTP 200 for
  the hosted page, exact proxy/profile identity, read-only profile attachment,
  terminal flow handling, and verified browser/connection/profile deletion.
- Real responses use `managed-auth.onkernel.com`, normalize expiry formatting,
  and omit the hosted URL after a terminal flow. Regression checks cover each.
- Synthetic probes used no real account credentials, SMS requests, Slack
  messages or purchases. Actual Gmail and merchant/SMS authentication require
  user participation and are not established by these probes.

Protected proof: `.local/kernel-only-20261008/managed-auth-tests-final-v2-20261009.json`.

## Activation

Activated after the previous gateway was healthy and idle. The reviewed drain
completed, old PID 57398 exited, and one replacement launch became healthy as
PID 66853. Slack's writer identity, fresh heartbeat and session store passed.
Frozen source and protected configuration stayed unchanged.

Post-activation checks confirmed Managed Auth initialized in the live database,
the authentication tool registered, local and public web health returned HTTP
200, and unauthenticated or foreign-origin requests were rejected. These checks
do not establish a real account login.

Two expired orphaned OTP collection items from the old implementation were
deleted with remote absence checks. Only their exact local request statuses
changed to cancelled. The saved Gmail login, other credentials and task context
were preserved.

Protected activation and post-check receipts:
`.local/kernel-only-20261008/managed-auth-activation-20261009.json` and
`.local/kernel-only-20261008/managed-auth-post-activation-20261009.json`.

Official contracts: [Managed Auth](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/auth/managed-auth),
[Hosted UI](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/auth/hosted-ui),
[SMS/email limitations](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/auth/faq), and
[profile concurrency](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/browsers/profiles/concurrency).
# Managed Auth hosted-link repair

Clanker's hosted login check rejected an owned login flow because Kernel serialized its expiry differently in the start and status responses. The start response had nine fractional digits; the status response rounded to six. Their exact difference was 137 nanoseconds. Python's timestamp parsing turned that into a one-microsecond difference, which failed the former equality check.

The connection, account owner, origin, profile, residential proxy, allowed domains, settings, and full hosted URL hash matched in the read-only production diagnosis. This failure happened before Clanker redirected the user to the hosted login page.

## Change

- Accept at most one microsecond of timestamp representation difference. Missing or invalid expiry values and larger differences remain blocked.
- Preserve all connection, ownership, profile, proxy, domain, hosted URL hash, cancellation, and generation checks.
- Label new Slack login buttons **Continue sign-in**, with the instruction: “Sign in to your account securely. I'll continue when you're signed in.”
- Request Slack authentication only after a 401. A backend 403 or 503 now offers retry and a return to Slack, without showing internal binding errors or another Slack login button. Expired links ask for a new link.

The implementation is shared across sites. No site selectors, account values, proxy exceptions, or alternate browser providers were added.

## Verification

The canonical Hermes runner passed **782 tests across 22 files**, with zero failures and unchanged frozen source. Regression cases cover nanosecond rounding, second rollover, truncation, reverse serialization order, reuse of a pending flow, terminal success/resume, authenticated browser binding, and rejection of differences beyond one microsecond.

The repaired production method verified the actual owned flow in a read-only check. By that time, Kernel reported `FAILED / COMPLETED / NEEDS_AUTH`; the hosted capability was no longer available. The old Slack link cannot reopen that ended attempt. A fresh user retry is required; Gmail sign-in itself has not been verified.

The live gateway was restarted once after source, configuration, process ownership, and idle checks. Post-activation checks confirmed a healthy connected Slack gateway, local and public web health, the exact repaired frontend asset, and continued rejection of unauthenticated and foreign-origin API requests. Protected configuration remained unchanged.

No credentials were read, login flows restarted, SMS requested, Slack messages sent, or purchases attempted during diagnosis and repair.

Protected local receipts are under `.local/kernel-only-20261008/`: `gmail-hosted-binding-precision-20261009.json`, `gmail-hosted-binding-repaired-20261009.json`, `managed-auth-tests-expiry-repair-20261009.json`, `managed-auth-expiry-repair-activation-20261009.json`, and `managed-auth-expiry-repair-post-activation-20261009.json`.

    status = request['upstream_status']
    return status is not None and status >= 300 and not (

    diagnostic = _active.get()
    return diagnostic if diagnostic is not None and diagnostic.client is client else None

    # Deletion and its verification read form one operation, including its error
    # reference. ContextVars keep concurrent requester operations independent.
    existing = current(client)
    if existing is not None:
        yield existing
        return
    diagnostic = KernelDiagnostic(client, name, task_id)
    token = _active.set(diagnostic)
    try:
        yield diagnostic
    finally:
        _active.reset(token)

    def __init__(self, client, name, task_id):
        self.client = client
        self.reference = uuid.uuid4().hex
        self.secrets = set()
        self.logged = False
        self.event = {'event': 'kernel_upstream_failure', 'provider': 'kernel',

            if isinstance(value, (str, int)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
                fields[name] = self.text(value)
            elif name == 'error' and isinstance(value, dict):

            self.remember_secret(authorization[7:])

            '/proxies/{id}/check' if re.fullmatch(r'/proxies/[^/]+/check', path) else

owns login discovery, password entry, account choices and interactive SMS/email
verification. There are no merchant-specific selectors, phone rewrites or retry
rules in this migration.

Clanker privately delivers an authenticated owner-only link and carries the
original task context internally. A pending flow is reused; starting another
login would cancel the old Kernel flow. The original task resumes only after the
same owned flow reports `SUCCESS` and its connection reports `AUTHENTICATED`.
Failed or expired flows need a fresh ordinary owner request, without an exact
approval phrase or automatic SMS loop.

Each workspace/requester/account/task has an isolated profile. Automation opens
a fresh browser with the successful snapshot and explicit `save_changes: false`.

checked before attachment. Cancellation, revocation and delayed cleanup cannot
revive a request or delete a replacement flow. Unconfirmed dispatch and cleanup
remain blocked for reconciliation.

from their write-only fields into Managed Auth credentials, so first sign-in may
require credentials again. Personal details and approved backend API-key
execution continue through Kernel Vault.

  unchanged. The first run caught a compatibility schema regression; the final
  run preserves the declarative, value-free legacy alias schema.

  terminal flow handling, and verified browser/connection/profile deletion.
- Real responses use `managed-auth.onkernel.com`, normalize expiry formatting,
  and omit the hosted URL after a terminal flow. Regression checks cover each.
- Synthetic probes used no real account credentials, SMS requests, Slack
  messages or purchases. Actual Gmail and merchant/SMS authentication require
  user participation and are not established by these probes.

Activated after the previous gateway was healthy and idle. The reviewed drain
completed, old PID 57398 exited, and one replacement launch became healthy as
PID 66853. Slack's writer identity, fresh heartbeat and session store passed.
Frozen source and protected configuration stayed unchanged.

Post-activation checks confirmed Managed Auth initialized in the live database,
the authentication tool registered, local and public web health returned HTTP
200, and unauthenticated or foreign-origin requests were rejected. These checks
do not establish a real account login.

Two expired orphaned OTP collection items from the old implementation were
deleted with remote absence checks. Only their exact local request statuses
changed to cancelled. The saved Gmail login, other credentials and task context
were preserved.

Protected activation and post-check receipts:
`.local/kernel-only-20261008/managed-auth-activation-20261009.json` and
`.local/kernel-only-20261008/managed-auth-post-activation-20261009.json`.

Official contracts: [Managed Auth](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/auth/managed-auth),
[Hosted UI](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/auth/hosted-ui),
[SMS/email limitations](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/auth/faq), and
[profile concurrency](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/browsers/profiles/concurrency).

The old Slack link cannot reopen that ended attempt. A fresh user retry is required; Gmail sign-in itself has not been verified.

Protected configuration remained unchanged.
